subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming separator contract use a complete in-band text repair, explicit boundary metadata, or a knowingly partial common-case text repair?
rationale: The bug and candidate fix location are clear, but the PR discussion and source show the near-maxChars case cannot be fully solved by naive text-only chunks without a maintainer choice about delivery limits and boundary semantics.

options.title: Consolidate a complete shared fix
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit boundary metadata
options.body: Ask the candidate PR to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split seam metadata through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if text-only chunks cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept partial common-case repair
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally land the common-case separator fix while leaving the exact near-limit boundary documented as remaining work on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Consolidate a complete shared fix
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation and require it to preserve paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across the current chunker/subscriber/coalescer layout plus earlier coalescing and chunking hardening work.
